lethal yellow (Ay), a mouse mutation in the agouti locus, is the result of the removal of all but the promoter region and noncoding first intron of a second gene, called Raly, that maps 280 kb distal to the agoutigenic gene.

the Ay mutation results in a fusion transcript between agouti and Raly, which encodes a chimeric agouti-Raly protein with a unique N-terminal agouti peptide sequence that is fused to the entire Raly protein sequence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Ay mutation is a complex rearrangement that removes the Raly gene and places the agouti promoter and noncoding exon 1 in an inverted orientation relative to the rest of the agout gene.
the agouti protein is the result of an RNA splicing event that joins two separate exons of the agoutic gene.

the Ay mutation is an example of a gene trap in which the Raly locus is trapped in the 3' untranslated region of the agoutic locus, which results in a chimeric transcript in which agouti is fused to Raly.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Ay allele is not a deletion, as has previously been assumed.
the Raly gene, and the deletion of Raly, are critical for understanding both the pleiotropic and recessive lethal effects of the Ay mutation.
the Ay mutation can serve as a model for the molecular mechanisms that underlie the genetic and phenotypical characteristics of other dominant pleiotropic mutations.
